collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 40 or older and another adult)

collection.description: A friend says a villager's hard years happened for a reason: say what they really think, or let it pass.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: There was a stretch of years in (subject)'s life that was very hard: illness, losses, one bad season after another. Today (friend), trying to be kind, says, "Well, I'm sure it all happened for a reason. It made you who you are." (subject) is quiet for a moment.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "I don't think it did," (subject) says, not unkindly. "It just happened. It was hard. I got through it. Some good things came after, and some came in spite of it. But it wasn't a lesson. It was just a bad time." (friend) is taken aback. Then (friend.he/she) nods. "I'm sorry I said that." "It's alright," says (subject). "People say it to be nice. I'd rather you just said it was hard." "It was hard," says (friend). "It was," says (subject).

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) doesn't argue. (subject.He/she) just says, "Maybe," and changes the subject. But later, alone, (subject.he/she) thinks about it. (subject.He/she) doesn't think there was a reason. (subject.He/she) thinks some things are just hard, and you get through them or you don't, and that's all. It's not a sad thought, exactly. It's honest. (subject.He/she) finds (subject.he/she) prefers it.
